claims.event: Wang Yande of Dongming, Kaifeng, served Taizong from childhood in charge of the kitchens, held up to five seals, became Zhaoxuan commissioner, compiled many records of court events, and died at sixty-four.
Great-grandfather of Wang Yande who served as magistrate of Puyang.
Grandfather of Wang Yande who served as recording adjutant of Xiangzhou.
Father of Wang Yande who led local leaders against the Khitan invasion late in the Jin and was on close terms with the Song founder’s father.
Song ruler who as governor of the capital trusted Wang Yande and Cheng Dexuan, and was brought to the throne by Wang Jien on the night of the founder’s death.
Inner attendant who announced the testament summoning Taizong to the throne, and with Wang Yande was made Zhaoxuan commissioner.
Topped out in commissioner ranks alongside Wang Yande and was made Zhaoxuan commissioner.
Song ruler on whose accession Wang Yande was reassigned to Huaizhou.

Chang Yanxin of Pingjin, Bingzhou, served on his grandfather’s staff, rebuilt the Tong Pass road, hunted bandits and subdued Chengzhou tribes as patrol commissioner in many prefectures, and died at sixty-four.
Grandfather of Chang Yanxin who under the Zhou governed Zhaoyi, Guide and Pinglu in turn.

Cheng Dexuan, styled Yuxi, a skilled physician, served Taizong, was summoned on the night of the founder’s death, braved a storm on the Huai to greet Chen Hongjin, and was demoted after Wang Renzan exposed his timber smuggling.
Came to court and was welcomed by Cheng Dexuan, who crossed the Huai in a storm to meet him.
Exposed Cheng Dexuan’s toll-evading timber rafts and inflated valuations.
Transport commissioner punished for letting Cheng Dexuan trade privately, demoted to right admonisher of the heir.
Transport commissioner of Jingxi punished for letting Cheng Dexuan trade privately.
Judge demoted to assistant of the Directorate of Works for letting Cheng Dexuan trade privately.

Metropolitan Patrol Commissioner of the Old Eastern Capital
Deputy Commandant of the Right Gate Guard
Deputy Commandant of the Right Guard
General of the Left Gate Guard
Right Admonisher of the Heir Apparent
Right Admonisher of the Heir Apparent
Assistant Director of the Directorate of Works

claims.event: Sent out as field marshal of Chongxin when his circle grew too large, later governed Huan with blank patents for frontier chiefs, moved to Feng during Li Shun’s revolt, and died at sixty-five.
Rebel in western Shu whose revolt led to Cheng Dexuan’s transfer to Fengzhou.
Song ruler who seated and questioned Cheng Dexuan on frontier affairs and promoted the second Wang Yande on his accession.
Son of Cheng Dexuan who memorialized for his father’s posthumous honors.
Elder brother of Cheng Dexuan who served in the princely household and became deputy commissioner of the inner wine bureau.
Second son of Cheng Dexuan who served as inner-palace honored guardsman.
Son of Cheng Deyuan who passed the jinshi examination and became erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
Wang Yande of Daming went as envoy to Gaochang with Bai Xun, wrote a record of the journey, was rebuked over Zhang Qixian’s intercession, rose to fiscal commissioner, and retired with wind paralysis.
Song ruler who sent Wang Yande and Bai Xun as envoys to Gaochang and rebuked Yande over the granary request.
Forecourt attendant sent with Wang Yande as envoy to Gaochang.
Chief minister who spoke for Wang Yande’s release from the granary and, disbelieved, kowtowed and confessed fault.
Erudite of the Directorate of Education who passed Wang Yande’s request to Zhang Qixian and later denied it.

label.en: Deputy Overall Commander of Bing and Dai
Deputy Commissioner of the Inner Wine Bureau
Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices

Chief Recipient of Edicts of the Bureau of Military Affairs
Grand General of the Left Qianniu Guard
General of the Left Martial Guard
Erudite of the Directorate of Education

claims.event: Disliked by contemporaries as an ambitious man who rose by currying favor; elder brother of Wang Yanzhi.
Elder brother of Wang Yande of Daming, a jinshi of Qiande 6 who retired as director of the agricultural lands bureau.
Wei Zhen, of unknown origin, was recommended by Yao Shu to Taizong, presented poems on auspicious timber, took Feihu and Yuzhou, governed many prefectures and died in Xianping 1.
Grandfather of Wei Zhen who served as salt monopoly commissioner of the Shanguo Army.
Father of Wei Zhen, magistrate of Putai, later relieved there by Yao Shu.
Relieved Wei Yue at Putai and as tutor of the princes praised Wei Zhen to Taizong.
Song ruler who summoned Wei Zhen to his princely residence and on campaign against Hedong camped at Zhenyang with Cao Bin.
Son of Wei Zhen who served as palace aide.

Zhang Zhi, styled Shoupu, orphan raised by his brother Zan, reckoned troop figures without error, graded Bureau clerks with Yin Derun, became associate director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and compiled the Essentials of Warfare.
Elder brother who raised the orphaned Zhang Zhi and served as reception clerk at the Bureau of Military Affairs.
Took notice of Zhang Zhi’s work in the military affairs section.
In charge of Bureau of Military Affairs business at Zhenyang, he noticed Zhang Zhi’s abilities.
Deputy attendant of the Rites Section who graded the Bureau clerks with Zhang Zhi at the Imperial Library Academy.

label.en: Director of the Bureau of Military Colonies
Salt Monopoly Commissioner of the Shanguo Army
Deputy Associate Director of the Section
General of the Left Gate Guard
Deputy Associate Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs
Grand General of the Left Garrison Guard
Grand General of the Right Divine Martial Army
Associate Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs
Reception Clerk of the Bureau of Military Affairs
Deputy Attendant of the Rites Section

claims.event: Practiced longevity arts, often served as itinerant palace commissioner on sacrifices and tours, and died of a stroke at seventy-four while awaiting audience at Chengming Hall.
Son of Zhang Zhi, an evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review, appointed vice director of the Court of Imperial Guards after his father’s death.
Grandson of Zhang Zhi appointed attendant-in-service of the Three Ranks after his grandfather’s death.

Yang Yungong of Mianzhu escaped Shu bandits by befriending their chief’s son, helped Ding Deyu, suppressed Guangzhou pirates including the Ye band, proposed Nan’an Military Prefecture, cleared Yangtze bandits despite a shoulder wound, and reorganized Jianghuai grain transport.
Commissioner of the Inner Reception Bureau who came to suppress the Shu bandits and appointed Yang Yungong after hearing his plan.
Song ruler who on Yang Yungong’s report made him chief inspection commissioner of Guang and Lian.

label.en: Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review
Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Guards
Recruitment and Inspection Commissioner of Mian and Han
Chief Inspection Commissioner of Guang and Lian
Deputy Commissioner of the Luo Park
Grand Transport Commissioner of Jianghuai and the Two Zhes
Commissioner of the Inner Reception Bureau

claims.event: Doubled grain deliveries to six million piculs, reformed the tea monopoly against Liu Shi’s proposal, created Wuwei Military Prefecture, banned private salt in Huainan, criticized Sichuan iron cash, and proposed Zhuge Liang’s wooden-ox carts for frontier supply.
Proposed abolishing the Yangtze tea monopoly offices to let merchants sell freely, opposed by Yang Yungong.
Salt and iron commissioner who endorsed Yang Yungong’s tea plan and later argued strongly for his view.
Deputy commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops appointed co-transport commissioner with Yang Yungong.
Assistant editor appointed co-transport commissioner who jointly directed tea and salt policy with Yang Yungong and Qin Xi.
Song ruler who after repeated petitions approved Yang Yungong’s Huainan salt ban.
Jointly directed tea and salt policy with Yang Yungong and Wang Ziyu, drafting new regulations.
Song ruler on whose accession Yang Yungong became commissioner of the Western Capital Left Treasury.
Deputy commissioner of honored ceremonial sent with Yang Yungong to survey the western frontier.
Gate usher sent with Yang Yungong and Dou Shenbao to survey and map the western frontier.
Earlier strategist whose wooden-ox carts Yang Yungong proposed for frontier grain transport.

label.en: Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops
Commissioner of the Western Capital Left Treasury
Transport Commissioner of the Huang and Imperial Canals
Deputy Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops

claims.event: Set up the horse-appraisal office, served as chief inspection commissioner of Jinghu, Jiang and Zhe during Wang Jun’s rebellion, died at Shengzhou aged fifty-six, and recommended Qin Xi for the Zhenzhou monopoly office.
Rebel whose uprising led the ruler to send Yang Yungong to guard against bandits in the south.
Inner Hall Honored Corps officer appointed Yang Yungong’s deputy as inspection commissioner.
Son of Yang Yungong sent to nurse him; a jinshi of Xianping 1 who governed five prefectures and rose to vice director in the Ministry of Justice.
Second son of Yang Yungong granted Academician Emeritus status on his father’s death, later vice director in the Ministry of Works.
Rebel during whose uprising Li Shun’s brother Zirong seized Mianzhu.
Rebel whose elder brother Zirong seized Mianzhu during Wang Xiaobo’s rebellion.
Elder brother of Li Shun who seized Mianzhu and was captured by Yang Yunsheng and Yang Yunyuan.
Elder brother of Yang Yungong who defeated Zirong at Mianzhu, became magistrate of his home county and later Right Admonisher of the Heir.
Younger brother of Yang Yungong who defeated Zirong, became magistrate of Shifang and later court reviewer.
Reported the Yang brothers’ capture of Zirong to court.

Qin Xi, styled Zhiyao, of Jiangning, presented Li Yu’s seals to Taizu, captured Ma Guanglian, ran the Huainan salt monopoly with Yang Yungong, governed Guangzhou, Suzhou and Quanzhou, and died at sixty-four.
Great-grandfather of Qin Xi who served as prefect of Yuezhou.
Grandfather of Qin Xi who was vice military commissioner of the Ningguo Army.
Father of Qin Xi, military supervisor of Jianzhou, who sent Xi to court with the seals on Li Yu’s surrender.
Southern Tang ruler whose surrender occasioned Qin Xi’s mission, and who appointed Xie Dequan deputy estate commissioner.
Song ruler who received Qin Xi and appointed him palace attendant.
Former Southern Tang officer turned outlaw in Jingchu, captured by Qin Xi.
Song ruler pleased by Qin Xi’s capture of Ma Guanglian.
Praised Qin Xi’s shrewdness and sent him to supervise tea affairs at Xingguo Army.
Song ruler who personally praised Qin Xi and chose him for Guangzhou.
Xie Dequan, styled Shiheng, of Fuzhou, repaired the Xianyang floating bridge, pacified the Yizhou tribes alone, improved granary storage and widened the capital’s streets against powerful opposition.
Father of Xie Dequan, magistrate of Houguan under the Wang, Southern Tang officer called Iron Dragon, who died defending Ezhou against Song.
Later Zhou ruler whose southern campaign saw Xie Wenjie reconnoiter enemy camps.
Transport commissioner who ordered Xie Dequan to repair the Xianyang floating bridge.
Sent to handle the Yizhou tribal revolt; reported Xie Dequan’s success.

claims.event: Opposed Xie Bi’s bid to detain great ministers, warned of the Khitan attack on Puyin, reformed Bian River dredging with an auger test, clashed with Liu Chenggui over palace construction, and died at Sizhou aged fifty-eight.
Malefactor who with the monk Chengya falsely accused chief ministers of colluding with Western Xia.
Monk who with Liu Ye brought a false accusation of collusion with Western Xia against chief ministers.
Examined the false accusation case and endorsed Xie Dequan’s defence of the great ministers.
Co-examiner of the accusation case who alone urged detaining great ministers, rebuked by Xie Dequan.
Commander who shut himself in his fort when the Khitan entered the passes, as cited by Xie Dequan.
Commander captured by the Khitan in their earlier incursion, as cited by Xie Dequan.
Planned eastern feng transport with Xie Dequan and Qi Lun and insisted on deep palace foundations over Dequan’s objections.
Ordered with Liu Chenggui and Xie Dequan to survey transport for the eastern feng sacrifice.
Son of Xie Dequan made registrar of Dingyuan after his father’s death.
Yan Rixin of Linhuan rose from clerk to frontier prefect, supported Zhang Ning’s raids, proposed limits on inherited stipends, welcomed the ruler at Fenyin and died aged sixty-eight.
Song ruler who on accession promoted Yan Rixin to palace attendant officer.
Deployment commander who raided tribal camps on the frontier with Yan Rixin’s support.
Jin Huaide of Gaotang passed the statutes examination and served as vice prefect of Xiang, Guang, Cang and Mo prefectures and prefect of De Prefecture.
Grandfather of Jin Huaide who served as palace attendant.
Father of Jin Huaide who served as magistrate of Yucheng.

label.en: Commissioner of the Western Dyeing Office
Grand General of the Right Leading Army Guard
Erudite of the Directorate of Education

claims.event: Held his city against the Khitan, renamed himself to avoid the name of Kou Zhun’s father, governed Qiong, Cang, Chan and Shan prefectures, and died aged seventy-three.
Transport commissioner who praised Jin Huaide’s governance during the Khitan invasion.
Military governor whose arrival at Mi Prefecture led to Jin Huaide being relieved.
Salt and iron commissioner who recommended Jin Huaide’s martial ability.
Judge who with Chen Shu recommended Jin Huaide’s martial ability.
Chief minister in whose circle Jin Huaide moved; Huaide changed his name because Zhun’s father shared it.
Transport commissioner who relayed the petition of Cang officials and people to keep Jin Huaide.
Song ruler who personally admonished Jin Huaide and promoted him to northern workshops commissioner.
Praised in the closing assessment as shrewd, with his tea, salt and transport proposals bringing considerable gain.
Praised in the closing assessment for devoted, alert service and cultured restraint.
Judged incorruptible but fond of authority, yet praised for rebuking Xie Bi over the dignity of great ministers.
Recalled in the closing assessment as rebuked by Xie Dequan over insulting great ministers.
